title: Reorder List
description:
Rearrange a singly linked chain by taking nodes alternately from its front and its back: first, last, second, second-to-last, and so on. Return the head of the rearranged chain. For odd lengths the center node appears last; for even lengths every node participates in a pair.

Change the links between existing nodes rather than changing their values. An empty chain returns an empty chain, and a one-node chain is unchanged. Repeated values are allowed, and each original node must appear exactly once: a cycle or an accidentally retained old link makes the result invalid.

The puzzle is that walking backward from the tail is not supported by a singly linked structure. Finding the midpoint, reversing the second half, and weaving the two halves together makes the required back-to-front order available without repeatedly rescanning for a predecessor.

Example 1:

Input: head = [1,2,3,4,5]
Output: [1,5,2,4,3]

Example 2:

Input: head = [1,2,3,4]
Output: [1,4,2,3]

Example 3:

Input: head = [8]
Output: [8]

Constraints:

  • 0 <= number of nodes <= 5,000.
  • -10,000 <= node.val <= 10,000.
